name: Question 11
problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.35$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ |

Given the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ above for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y,$ calculate $P(X<2).$
worked_solution:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.35$ | $0.1$ | $0.45$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.55$ | $0.45$ | $1$ |

The marginal mass function for $X$ is given in the following table:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.35$ | $0.45$ | $0.2$ |

Finally, using the table of values of the marginal mass function for $X,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & =P(X\in {0,1}) \\  & =P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\  & =0.35+0.45 \\  & =0.8.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

If the random variables X and Y have joint distribution with joint probability mass function f(x,y), then we have

P(X=x)=fX(x)=∑yf(x,y)P(Y=y)=fY(y)=∑xf(x,y)

where fX(x) and fY(y) are the marginal mass functions for X and Y, respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for X corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for Y corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

X=0 0.15 0.2 0.35

fY 0.55 0.45 1

P(X<2)=P(X∈{0,1})=P(X=0)+P(X=1)=0.35+0.45=0.8.
